einzeiler: Why so many people believe in ghosts and how the human brain creates paranormal…
kurzfassung: Three-quarters of Americans believe in paranormal activity, yet psychology professor Melissa Maffeo argues that these encounters are often the result of cognitive biases, priming, and sleep paralysis. Listeners share personal ghost stories and premonitions, which science attributes to pattern-seeking behavior and reconstructive memory. While skeptics emphasize rational explanations, researchers acknowledge that human perception captures only a fraction of physical reality.
stichpunkte: Around 75 percent of Americans believe in some form of paranormal activity.
Melissa Maffeo explores the psychology behind supernatural beliefs in her book The Science of the Supernatural.
Sleep paralysis occurs during REM sleep when the brain wakes up while muscles remain immobilized, often triggering hallucinations or the feeling of a presence.
Listeners share diverse personal accounts of ghosts, apparitions of deceased relatives, and striking premonitions.
Experiments by anomalistic psychologist Chris French show that belief and expectation heavily influence whether people report supernatural phenomena.
Cognitive biases, shared cultural touchpoints, and the human desire for narrative-building shape how people interpret ambiguous sensory experiences.
Although science lacks definitive proof for ghosts, researchers concede that human physiology detects only a tiny fraction of existing physical stimuli.

clips.hook: If three-quarters of people believe in ghosts, we should study it
clips.text: If the vast majority of the population believes in the paranormal and turns out to be correct, investigating it would reveal a great deal about the world.

clips.hook: Why sleep paralysis makes your body feel trapped
clips.text: Roughly one-fifth of the population wakes up during REM sleep while their muscles remain paralyzed, causing the brain to send movement signals that the body ignores.

clips.hook: A mysterious folding chair in an empty basement
clips.text: A business owner found a metal folding chair in the middle of a locked basement, only to learn later that a firefighter had previously died by suicide in that exact spot.

clips.hook: The surprising results of a haunted room experiment
clips.text: When researchers tested whether electromagnetic fields and infrasound caused supernatural feelings, they discovered no actual link between those physical forces and reported anomalies.

clips.hook: We only experience a tiny fraction of physical reality
clips.text: Humans lack the physiological tools to detect most physical stimuli in the world, raising the slight possibility that undiscovered phenomena could eventually be measured.

beschreibung:
One in 5 Americans say they've seen a ghost. But what if it was really our brain that had tricked us into thinking we saw something we didn't?

In the "Science of the Supernatural" psychology professor Melissa Maffeo argues how a paranormal experience could be our brains just misinterpreting the external world.
